subject: res-ipc-endpoints
text: - **Linux / macOS:** Unix domain socket file `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory (security-plan arch amendment 2): `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/viola/` on macOS, and `/tmp/viola-<uid>/` only as a fallback; never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root. The socket is chmod 0600 after the bind. The start arbiter is the sibling `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.lock`: `run` holds an exclusive lock on it, and a held lock is the taken-name refusal. `run` resolves the path once and records it as `endpoint` in the instance snapshot. Every other process (`hook`, `mcp`, CLI verbs, and `run`'s collision check) connects to the recorded `endpoint`, because processes spawned inside the session may run with a different environment from the wrapper. Each reads the snapshot through `viola_state::replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, and only a snapshot read whole yields an `endpoint`, because one rebuilt from the log carries no `endpoint`, `pid` or `started_at`: on a replay, an absence or an error `live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs and `mcp`'s frame tools) returns none; on a replay or an absence hook `connect` is unreachable (fail open; SessionEnd appends directly); `run`'s collision check takes its caller's one read and decides a replay from the heartbeat alone (`already-live` within `STALE_AFTER`, else free) and an absence or an error as free. None rebuilds the path. Linux abstract-namespace names are never used, because they carry no filesystem permissions and any local user could connect (see Local endpoint trust boundary).

subject: res-ipc-endpoints
text: - Before its first frame each process that connects to the recorded `endpoint`, but `run`'s collision check (`hook`'s event and dialog paths, the CLI frame verbs `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, and `mcp`'s four frame tools), checks that the process serving it is the snapshot's wrapper: the connected stream's peer pid (`viola_channel::Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid`) and its OS start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness). A mismatch or a check that cannot be made sends no frame: CLI exit 21 `instance-unreachable`, MCP `instance-unreachable`, the hook failing open. macOS reports no peer pid and stays on the recorded gap.

subject: res-binaries
res-binaries
text: - Subcommands: `run`, `revive`, `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `hook <event>`, `mcp`, `verify`, `pause`, `release` (incl. `--budget`), `link`, `unlink`, `plugin install`. `mcp` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) is hidden from `viola --help` (`#[command(hide = true)]`: run by the plugin, never by a person) and takes no argument but the global `--home`; it serves the five tools over stdio until stdin closes, and exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr and no role file when its home or `diagnostics/` (each that exists) fails `viola_state::strict::check_path`. `verify` takes `[--record <DIR>] [-- <program> [args…]]` (program default `claude`). `list` takes `[--json]` and nothing else; it exits 0 with a board (one stdout write), 21 when its strict-modes check refuses the home, `instances/` or any one instance (the whole board refused), 1 for an internal error through the `cli` catch site and 2 for a clap usage error (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list). `plugin install` takes `[--json]` and nothing else (`viola plugin` alone is a clap usage error; clap's own `viola plugin help` is served); it exits 0 with its result (one stdout write), 21 when its strict-modes check refuses the home or any existing `marketplace/` tree dir (nothing created, no log opened), 1 for an internal error through the `cli` catch site and 2 for a clap usage error. `revive` takes `<name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [-- <child args>]`, or `<name> --list`, each with `[--json]`; under `--json` a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal is the exit-1 `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document (one of the five codes, §Standard Contracts) with stderr empty, and `--list --json` prints the `ok.sessions` document, or the `no-session` document with exit 1; it exits 0 when the revived child's wrapper ends as `run`'s does, 1 for a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal and 2 for a clap usage error (a malformed `--id` included).

subject: res-binaries
text: - `link` and `unlink` each take `<driver> <driven> [--json]` (one shared `LinkArgs`), the verb's instance being the driven one; each exits 0 with its one result line, or `{"v":1,"ok":<ok>}` under `--json` (`link`: `{since, already_linked}`; `unlink`: `{}`), 21 when the instance check refuses, no live endpoint is recorded or the serving process is not the recorded wrapper, 20 for a wrapper error (a `-32602` included, such as `driver` equal to `driven`), and 1 for a refusal reply or an `ok` of another shape.

subject: res-binaries
text: - `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` exit 21 when their instance check refuses, as `link` / `unlink` do (human: the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr; `--json`: the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document on stdout). `verify` exits 1 with the home-state pair, before its `cli` log and any step line, when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/`, or `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`. `run` and `revive`'s start exit 1 before any log when the home-tree check refuses (`revive --json` keeps its `strict-modes-failed` document). How a home under a regular file reads on each OS: Filesystem, `instances/<ViolaName>/`, below.

subject: res-binaries
text: - Hidden flags: `hook <event> --capture <DIR> [--answers <DIR>]` — `viola verify`'s probe capture arm ([Hook Contract]): an absolute, existing `<DIR>` only; stdin capped at `MAX_FRAME` and written raw to an exclusively claimed `<DIR>/<PascalEvent>.<k>.json`; `--answers` (inert without `--capture`) makes a dialog event print the one `decision_body` its `take(64)`-read closed `ProbeAnswer` id selects, and nothing on any failure; no `VIOLA_*` read, no obs init, no channel; always exit 0 with empty stderr. Its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]` (`cmd::hook::capture_statusline`, sole caller Run B's probe settings) takes the same `<DIR>` and stdin bounds, refuses stdin past `MAX_FRAME`, files the payload raw at the first free `StatusLine.<k>.json` and `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holding exactly `bin-sh` or `other` (a missing word is `other`, the word written nowhere), prints nothing and reads no `budget.json` or snapshot; `--shell` on any other arm changes nothing.

subject: res-claude-integration
text: - Flags passed to the child: `--plugin-dir <viola home>/plugin/<version>-<hash>`, first on every start; then `--settings <instance dir>/settings.json` when the start wrote a settings override (none on Windows, and none for a pinned path the override rule refuses; see the next bullet); then the caller's arguments. The flag is the agent crate's constant, `viola_agent_claude::statusline::SETTINGS_FLAG`, and `run` uses it. `viola verify`'s Runs C and D read the same constant, and verify's default program reads `viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM` (both moved at chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup). A revived start launches the program `claude` (`viola_agent_claude::PROGRAM`, looked up by name on the reviving process's own `PATH` by `run`'s resolver) and, after those flags, adds `--resume <id>`, then `--fork-session` when `--fork` is given, then the words after `--` (`viola_agent_claude::resume_args`; that crate is the one product home of the two flag literals). The id is one argv element of a direct spawn: the newest logged id of the session-id shape (`is_session_id`: 36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18 and 23, ASCII hex elsewhere), or `--id` when the instance's log holds it. A logged value on the child's command line is a crossing the founder ratified (live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the overseer), shown to him as a crossing with two options: ratify it, or allow only an id the human types.

subject: res-claude-integration
text: - `viola verify`'s probe plugin `viola-verify-probe`, written only under `ledger/probes/<pid>/plugin/`: four exec-form hooks on the pinned path (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd, each `hook <event> --capture <probe>/captures`; `timeout: 5` on all but SessionEnd). Its child flags: `-p "<PROBE_PROMPT>" --model haiku --plugin-dir <probe>/plugin --no-session-persistence`, cwd the probe dir. The dialog-kind probe plugin adds PreToolUse (matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`), PermissionRequest and PostToolUse to the four spine hooks, the two dialog events carrying `--answers <root>/answers`. verify's five interactive children follow the print probe, each a direct `<program>` spawn at 80×24 under the R8 strip with no key written into a CLI dialog: Run A with cwd a fresh OS-temp `viola-verify-*` dir; Run B with cwd `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` and, on Unix for shell-plain paths, `--settings <probe dir>/typed/statusline.json` after its `--plugin-dir` pair (no flag on Windows); Run C (`--model haiku --settings <DIALOG_SETTINGS>`, the dialog plugin) with cwd `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/`; Run D (`--model haiku --permission-mode plan --settings {"plansDirectory":"<Run D dir>/plans"}`, the dialog plugin) with cwd `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/`; Run E (the run args, then `--plugin-dir` and the capture plugin under `<probe dir>/resume/`, then `--resume <id>` built by `viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)`, its second caller beside `viola revive`, the id being Run B's first SessionStart `session_id` admitted by `is_session_id` through `ledger::resume_target`, one argv element; no `--settings`, input empty) with cwd `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/`.

subject: res-claude-integration
text: - Per-session settings override: `instances/<ViolaName>/settings.json` holds `{"statusLine":{"type":"command","command":"<pinned path> hook statusline"}}`, the path absolute, so the child's status line is viola's wrapper. `viola run` rewrites it whole at every start, a revived start included, through `viola_state::fs::replace_private` at 0600, after the first snapshot and before the spawn. It is written only on Unix, and only when every character of the pinned path is an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `_ - . / :` (`viola_agent_claude::statusline::override_document`); for any other path, and on Windows, no override is written and no `--settings` is passed. That the child takes a `statusLine` given through `--settings` is the ledger row `statusline-override` (probed by Run B's probe `--settings`, relied on Unix only, since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows; §Cross-cutting Patterns, Capability ledger). A code-bearing file written at every start and handed to the CLI is a boundary widening the founder ratified (live, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the operator). The Windows override is owed to the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements".

subject: res-env-vars
text: - `VIOLA_DIR`: the absolute path of the instance's state directory (`<viola home>/instances/<ViolaName>/`), set by `viola run` in the child. It is read by `hook` (for the recorded `endpoint`, the SessionEnd direct-append fallback, the statusline wrapper and the diagnostics directory) and by `mcp` and every CLI verb run inside the session. Each derives the viola home as the grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR`, so a session started with `--home` keeps its hooks, MCP server and nested CLI calls in that home. As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract), `hook` and every CLI verb, `run` and `revive` included, read it: the verbs through `resolved_home`, which takes the `VIOLA_DIR` grandparent only when `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` pass `instance_of`'s shape check, a pair that fails falling through to the default, never refusing (§Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management); `viola mcp` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) resolves its home through the same `resolved_home` and reads `VIOLA_NAME` for its own name (the `from` it adds and its detail sink).

subject: res-env-vars
text: - `hook`'s event, dialog and statusline paths (not its two `--capture` arms) take `VIOLA_DIR` through `instance_of`, then `canonical`, then `trusted` (`check_instance`), before anything under the home is read: a `VIOLA_DIR` naming an instance directory that does not exist canonicalises to no session, so `viola hook` exits 0 and writes nothing.

text:
- Removed from the child's environment (R8, operator ruling 2026-09-25): every inherited `CLAUDE*` name (ASCII case-insensitive on Windows, exact on Unix) except a name the user defines persistently — on Windows a value NAME under `HKCU\Environment` or `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment` (read through windows-sys Registry, names only), on Unix a name in `config.json` `claude_env_keep`. The identity floor (`viola-agent-claude` `IDENTITY_FLOOR`, a ledger row; the 11 names measured on the Windows host: `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `CLAUDE_PID`) is removed whatever the persistent environment says. Names only: the strip, the registry reader and the logs never read a value; `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` names the stripped (`env_stripped_known`) and the kept (`env_kept`) names. Two Linux dev-host readings stand beside the floor's Windows origin (as measured at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/scratch-session.md`, names only). The tool environment PATH `claude` 2.1.289 hands a session holds 10 `CLAUDE*` names, all on the floor (`CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID` absent). The environment 2.1.287 hands a hook, read in a child started with every inherited `CLAUDE*` name removed, holds 12: eight of the eleven (absent: `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`) and four outside them (`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`).
 The floor stays the eleven: those four are not identity names (the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-07T11:37Z, relayed by the overseer), and the prefix rule already removes them whenever they are inherited outside the persistent set. The readings came from a scratch hook, not a `viola verify` probe, so the floor's ledger row stays owed.

subject: res-env-vars
text:
- Test-harness only, never read by `viola`:
  - `AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE`: an explicit override of `run --mutants`' diff base, read by `viola-harness` (`run_cmd`). Without it the harness derives the base from git history (the last master flip before the chunk's oldest operator pre-CI commit; test-plan §3 `run` step 4). No CI workflow sets it: `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml` run no mutation job, and the dispatch-only `windows-mutants.yml` runs the `--package <member> --file …` arm, which reads no base.
  - `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES`: `1` keeps `target/e2e-home/` homes for the CI gates. Read by `viola-harness`, by the root test chain (`tests/support/home.rs`) and by viola-e2e's `harness::session` guard (`HarnessSession`'s `Drop`, through `keep_home`), which keeps the session's home under `1`.
  - `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED`: `1` keeps a failing test's home for post-mortem. Read by the root test chain (`tests/support/home.rs` `keep_decision`), by viola-e2e's `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` `Booted` guard, which keeps a booted session's home only when the value is `1` and the thread is panicking, and by viola-e2e's `harness::session` guard, whose `Drop` (after its `cleanup`) keeps the home when `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1`, or when this value is `1` and the thread is panicking (chunk 2026-10-17-end-to-end-path-binary-and-harness-legs). `run --mutants` sets it to `0` on the `cargo mutants` command.
  - `CI`: read by `viola-harness` for presence only (`std::env::var_os("CI").is_some()` in the bin and in `run::run`, passed to `run_with` as `ci`). Its one effect: `run --local-live` under it returns `{"v":1,"cmd":"run","ok":false,"reason":"live-in-ci"}`, exit 2, before any build, spawn or suite, so the real `claude` never runs in CI.

text:
- Test seams, read only by a `viola` built with the test-only `fake-agent` feature (never by a release build):
  - `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS`: `#[cfg(feature = "fake-agent")] fn hold_pump_start` in `src/cmd/run.rs` parses it as u64 milliseconds, capped at 5 000, and holds the pump back after the child starts, so `tui_host_resize_in_the_pump_start_window_reaches_the_child` can land a host resize between the spawn sizing and the pump's first look. A test seam, not a configuration channel: it disables no control and widens no redaction. Ratified by the operator at the 2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate wrap (security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns carve-out).
  - `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC`: `#[cfg(feature = "fake-agent")] fn panic_if_asked` in `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs` (the module is declared without a cfg; its fns carry it) reads it, and `hook()` calls it right after `viola_obs_init`, before the stdin lock. It panics only when the value is exactly `1` (`0`, `false`, `off`, empty, absent and anything else return), with the fixed ASCII payload `"forced-hook-panic ".repeat(256)` (4 608 B, no upstream text, path or secret), so the panic sink holds the instance: one codes-only `event:"panic"` role line in `diagnostics/hook-<name>.ndjson` and one `detail-hook.ndjson` line over 4 KiB, exit 0, empty stdout and stderr. The variable is named in product source only in that file. A test seam, not a configuration channel: it disables no control and widens no redaction. Ratified by the founder live on 2026-09-28, together with the G2 exact-path exemption for its panic lines (security-plan Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, test seam).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `config.json`: user settings (the budget thresholds `five_hour` and `seven_day`, two top-level keys, each a JSON whole number from 0 to 100, defaults 90 and 85, read by the wrapper once at its start through its own `MAX_FRAME`-capped read, so a changed file is seen at the next start, and by `viola list` at each run through the same `run::budget::read_thresholds` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list), whose bad keys log the same line into `cli-<name>.ndjson` under a `VIOLA_NAME` only; a value that is no whole percentage, such as `101`, `-1`, `"90"`, `90.5` or `null`, takes that key's default while the other key stands, each bad key is one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}` WARN line in `run-<name>.ndjson`, and no value of either switches the gate off; `diagnostics_level`: `"info"` by default, or `"debug"`; `claude_env_keep`: the Unix R8 pass-list, an array of at most 32 names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, default empty — a bad value is rejected whole, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect; `dialog_hold_s`: the dialog hold, a JSON whole number of seconds from 60 to 3600, default 60, read by the wrapper once at its start through `run::dialog::read_hold` right after the thresholds, any other value taking 60 with one `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json", detail:"malformed"}` WARN line, so no value makes the hold zero or unbounded). It is read with a `MAX_FRAME` cap and must carry `v` = 1. An unusable file or value falls back to the default and is reported as a `parse-rejected{parser:"config-json"}` line.

res-filesystem
text: - A snapshot the replay rebuilds from the log writes one `state-recovered` line into the role file of the process that read it (`cli-<name>.ndjson`, `mcp.ndjson`, `hook-<name>.ndjson` or `run-<name>.ndjson`), from each replay reader: `live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs and `mcp`'s frame tools), hook `connect`, statusline `serve` and `run`'s collision check, beside `viola revive` and `viola list`. `viola revive`'s preflight reads the snapshot once for both its collision check and its recorded-directory reading, so one replay writes one line.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `open_role_file` and `write_detail` (`src/obs.rs`) run `strict::check_diagnostics` on an existing `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything: a symbolic link is refused, a folder takes the read rule, a file takes the read rule on Unix and the write rule on Windows, and an absent path passes. A refusal is a failed open: the writer ends at `std::io::sink`, and a detail line is dropped.

subject: res-filesystem
text:
- `instances/<ViolaName>/events.ndjson`, `events.ndjson.lock`, `snapshot.json`, `snapshot.json.lock`, `heartbeat`, `settings.json` (the per-session settings override that wraps the statusline; Unix only, see Claude Code integration names), `diagnostics/` (the owner-only content-bearing detail files `detail-<role>.ndjson`, such as the panic payload and backtrace in `detail-run.ndjson`; dir 0700, files 0600 on Unix; one `write` per line; file format owned by obs and fixed by `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`. Codes-only process lines go to the home-level role files). v1 never rotates or truncates `events.ndjson`, because `wait`'s `after` and `send`'s `cursor` are byte offsets into it. Bounding its size is an open item, and any scheme must keep existing offsets valid. These entry points check these files before they use them: `viola list`; `viola revive`; `viola run`'s start (through `check_home_tree` with its name); `viola hook`'s statusline, event and dialog paths (sharing `trusted`); `viola mcp`'s frame tools; and the CLI frame verbs `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (sharing `client::refuse_untrusted`). `viola list` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `viola_state::board::scan` runs `check_path` on the home and on `instances/`, each that exists (absent passes, an unstattable one is refused), reads each entry's type without following a link (a link, a non-directory or a name that is no `ViolaName` gives no instance and is only counted), joins a path only from a parsed name, then runs `check_instance` per instance in name order, all before any file under the home is opened and before its log starts; the first failure refuses the whole board with exit 21 (`--json`: `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr empty; human: the instance-state or the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr, stdout empty), no log opened, no line written and the home's mode left as found — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13).
 `viola revive` (the start arm and `--list`) runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` over the home (the read rule), `instances/` (the write rule), the instance directory (the read rule), its `diagnostics/` (the read rule), its `snapshot.json` (the write rule) and its `events.ndjson` (the write rule on Unix, the read rule on Windows), each that exists and a folder before what it holds, before its wrapper log opens, and a refusal is exit 1 with the state-files `unable:` / `hint:` pair (under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty): no log opened, no line written (no `process-start`, no `process-exit`), no child started and the home's mode left as found. `viola hook statusline` runs the same check on its canonicalised instance directory before anything under the home is read or opened; a refused instance returns exit 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file opened, no `hook-invoked` or `hook-decision` line, no stdin read, no command run, nothing printed and `budget.json` untouched. Neither arm writes the word `strict-modes-failed` on any line. `viola link` / `viola unlink` run `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` before `client::start`, so before any role file or log opens and before any snapshot value is read; a refusal is exit 21 (`--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty; human the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr), no line written and the mode left as found. Each of these checks comes first because opening a log sets an existing home to 0700 (as measured on the statusline arm at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through, `evidence/red-green.md` §3), and a check made after it passes a home at 0770. Both orders were fixed at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor: before it `revive`'s start arm opened its log first, and a home at 0770 came back 0700 and passed the check (as measured at that chunk's `research.md`, runs C and D, and `evidence/red-green.md` (a)), and the statusline arm opened its log after a refused check, so its refusal lasted one invocation (`evidence/red-green.md` (b)). That a refused check leaves no trace on the statusline arm is the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13). `check_instance` has these three product call sites (`src/cmd/hook.rs` `trusted`, shared by the statusline, event and dialog paths; `src/cmd/revive.rs`; and `src/cmd/client.rs` `refuse_untrusted`, shared by `link` / `unlink` and the six frame verbs; the rule: `check_instance(` under `src/`). Outside that rule `viola-mcp`'s `tools.rs` `frame` calls it, and `run`'s start reaches its set through `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree`.
 The check is proven on Unix (five widened modes). On Windows `cfg(windows)` cases prove it: an instance tree granted Users write is refused `Writable` beside a `create_private_dir` tree that passes, a `diagnostics/` granted Users read is refused, and a plain home made before viola is refused, naming its inherited Users (`S-1-5-32-545`) write entry (as measured at ci#40403389629, `windows-2025`).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `viola_state::strict` holds two rules. The read rule is the write rule plus, on Unix, a refusal of any group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`) and, on Windows, a refusal of any allow ACE, an inherit-only one included, that grants a right in `READ_RIGHTS` (`0x9000_0001`: `FILE_READ_DATA` | `GENERIC_READ` | `GENERIC_ALL`) to a SID `trusted_sid` rejects (`unix_read_verdict`, `windows_read_verdict`, `check_read`). `Refused` holds `Readable` for a read-rule refusal and `Symlink` for a symbolic link `check_diagnostics` meets, each with a fixed message.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, name, key)` checks the home (the read rule); with a name, `check_instance`'s set; then `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`; with a key, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola` (`viola.exe` on Windows), `plugin/<key>/`, its `hooks/` and its `.claude-plugin/` (the write rule). - `budget.json` + `budget.json.lock`: the newest `rate_limits` reading across wrapped sessions, timestamped, last-writer-wins. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through) the file is `{"v":1,"five_hour":…,"seven_day":…,"read_at":"<RFC 3339 UTC, milliseconds>"}`. A window is the word `"unknown"` or `{used_percentage, resets_at}`, and either field may be `"unknown"`. It is replaced whole through `replace_private` at 0600 under an exclusive lock on `budget.json.lock` (`viola_state::budget::write_budget`). Written only by `hook statusline`, and only when the payload holds a `rate_limits` object, so a payload without one leaves the last reading standing. Read by each wrapper's budget gate ([Budget Governor]), and by `list` for its payload's top-level `budget`. The file has one checked read, `viola_state::budget::read_budget_stamped(home) -> Option<StampedReading>` (`{reading, read_at}`; chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list), with two product paths: the gate's `read_budget(home) -> Option<BudgetReading>` (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), now `read_budget_stamped(home).map(|s| s.reading)`, and `viola list`. `read_at` is `"unknown"` when the key is absent or no string. The read runs, in order: `strict::check_path` on the home, `check_path` on `budget.json`, a shared lock on `budget.json.lock`, the bytes through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` (over the cap is no reading), a tolerant parse that skips an unknown key, and no reading unless `v` is 1. Every failure is no reading, with no log line. It never writes `budget.json`, and an absent file under a home that passes its check creates nothing, the lock sibling included.
 The wrapper refusing a driver on this file, which a hook arm writes and the trusted-file list does not hold, is a boundary widening the founder ratified: his own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, ratifies it as built — read behind the strict-modes check on the home and the file, failing open (it had landed on the operator's word, 2026-10-10, which is no ratification; superseded 2026-10-13) (security-plan §Authentication & Authorization, `~/.viola/` access control).
